data.title: Chances of Fed Rate Hike Rise After Strong Jobs Numbers — WSJ
data.description:
By WSJ Staff

The chances of a Federal Reserve interest-rate increase next month bumped up to about 78%, from 67% yesterday, according to CME FedWatch data.

The increase happened after a strong jobs report that suggested that the central bank's focus will remain squarely on inflation. U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, beating a Wall Street Journal consensus of 59,000. The numbers for August and September were revised up by a combined 84,000. The unemployment rate slipped to 4.1%. Read more about the bond market's reaction to the jobs data here.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

The commission said that finding such a buyer fully addresses the EU's competition concerns.

data.title: Late Payments Steal Affirm's Earnings Spotlight. Wall Street Sees More Run to Run. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mariapaula Gonzalez

Investors looked past Affirm's stellar earnings to fret over a critical metric.

"That delinquency rate, man," Seaport Research analyst Jeff Cantwell wrote in a note late Thursday.

Affirm reported Thursday that its 30-day late payments rose to 2.9% of monthly installment loans in the fiscal first quarter ended Sept. 30, up nine basis points from last year and up 35 basis points from the fourth quarter.

Investors have historically been unforgiving of worsening borrower credit trends, Cantwell noted. The firm has a Neutral rating on the stock.

Adding fuel to the fire, October's blowout U.S. jobs report rekindled expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December, a headwind that has continued to pressure fintechs' valuations. For Affirm, higher interest rates could increase funding costs and credit risks.

Affirm shares dropped 3.7% to $67.06 on Friday, bringing its 12-month decline to roughly 7%, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Still, some Wall Street analysts say the credit anxieties have been overblown. Susquehanna analyst James Friedman wrote that Affirm's delinquency trends remain manageable, emphasizing that projected loan defaults sit comfortably within historical norms.

Not to mention that the company's other numbers looked strong.

Gross merchandise volume, a measure of all transactions processed on Affirm's platform within a specific period, grew 34% to $14.4 billion in the fiscal first quarter, beating analysts' consensus calls for $14 billion.

Revenue surged 35% to $1.26 billion in the period, above analysts' consensus estimate of $1.21 billion. Adjusted earnings of 47 cents a share topped Wall Street's estimates of 38 cents a share.

Analyst Gus Gala at Monness, Crespi, Hardt sees Affirm's post-earnings stock pullback as a buying opportunity, noting that its underlying revenue momentum has outpaced management's conservative outlook.

Affirm bumped its full-year outlook for gross merchandising volume to more than $65.25 billion, up from a previous call for above $64 billion. Gala pointed out that this forecast models GMV growth slowing to around 28%, even though October growth ran in the high-30% range. He raised Affirm's price target to $95 from $90 while maintaining a Buy rating.

Fueling much of that GMV growth was the Affirm Card, a hybrid Visa debit card that connects to a customer's bank, Susquehanna analyst James Friedman wrote late Thursday. Active cardholders soared 112% to 6 million in the fiscal first quarter, now making up 21% of all Affirm users. Card purchase volume also hit $3.3 billion, driving nearly all direct-to-consumer growth. Friedman has a Positive rating and $110 price target on Affirm stock.

Analysts have an average price target of $97.73 for Affirm, implying about a 40% upside from Thursday's closing price of $69.66.

Write to Mariapaula Gonzalez at mariapaula.gonzalez@barrons.com

data.title: Brazilian banks cut growth forecasts, raising fiscal stakes for Lula
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bradesco cuts Brazil's 2027 GDP forecast to +0.4%
  • Investment platform XP sees economic growth up 0.3% next year
  • Downgrades follow similar revisions by Itau and BTG
  • Weaker growth adds to budget headache for reelected Lula

By Marcela Ayres

Brazil's top lenders have slashed their economic growth forecasts for next year, threatening reelected President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's pledge to honor his campaign spending promises while also returning the budget to surplus.

When it submitted the budget bill for next year to Congress in August, Lula's leftist administration projected gross domestic product growth of 2.46% in 2027.

Economists now see activity expanding at a mere fraction of that pace as uncertainty about Lula's next government, high interest rates and tighter financial conditions weigh on demand.

Bradesco, one of Brazil's leading banks, lowered its 2027 GDP forecast to 0.4% on Friday and brokerage and financial platform XP cut its estimate to 0.3%. Both were previously expecting growth of 1.0% next year.

The revisions mirrored moves by Itau, Brazil's largest lender, and BTG Pactual, which last week reduced their GDP growth forecasts to 0.5% and 0.6%, respectively.

All four cited expectations that Brazil's punishing interest rates — the central bank ended a run of cuts this week and kept its benchmark rate at 13.75% — will remain elevated for longer due to a worsening inflation outlook.

Growth within the range of the four forecasts would mark the weakest performance in Latin America's largest economy since 2016, excluding 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic hit.

It also would add to longstanding concerns over gross debt levels of nearly 83% of GDP — or 95.2% under the International Monetary Fund's metrics — well above most emerging-market peers.

BROAD SELLOFF

Lula's surprise victory over right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro in an October 25 runoff election triggered a sharp weakening of Brazil's real currency and a surge in long-term borrowing costs.

"The combination of tighter financial conditions, weaker confidence and slower credit growth should deepen the loss of momentum over coming quarters," Bradesco said.

More immediately, the weaker outlook heightens the stakes for Lula as he considers his next government's economic program.

With mandatory public spending climbing rapidly, the government has relied heavily on assumptions of stronger tax revenue growth to improve public finances. A sharper-than-expected economic slowdown would undermine that strategy.

The Finance Ministry said it was reviewing its macroeconomic assumptions and could not comment before the expected release of its updated forecasts later this month.

In a fiscal risk report released this week, the Treasury said GDP growth was "the largest source of uncertainty for revenue estimates," calculating that every 1-percentage-point shortfall in growth would cut federal tax revenues by 16.6 billion reais ($3.02 billion).

Before the recent deterioration in the outlook, the government had projected an effective primary surplus of 18.6 billion reais in 2027, equivalent to 0.13% of GDP and the first effective surplus since 2022.

That projection was made before Lula issued several election campaign pledges, including a larger Bolsa Familia welfare program, direct payments to micro-entrepreneurs and expanded student benefits.

Each of the four institutions that cut their GDP forecasts continues to project a primary deficit next year, ranging from 0.1% to 0.6% of GDP.

BTG said the outlook would depend heavily on whom Lula chooses for his economic team as well as his fiscal strategy.

"The intensity of the slowdown itself depends on the fiscal response," it said.

($1 = 5.5039 reais)

data.title: Oil export boom lifts Brazil trade surplus above forecasts in October
data.description:
Brazil's trade surplus topped forecasts in October, driven by a surge in oil shipments and firmer commodity prices, official data showed on Friday.

Latin America's largest economy posted a trade surplus of $9.3 billion for the month, said the Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade and Services, above the $9.1 billion expected by analysts in a Reuters poll.

  • Exports rose 20.0% from a year earlier to $37.8 billion, while imports increased 14.8% to $28.5 billion

  • "It was the largest monthly trade flow on record, with both exports and imports reaching all-time highs," said Herlon Brandao, the ministry's director of trade statistics

  • Crude oil was the standout performer, with exports soaring 122.6% to $8.5 billion, making it the single largest contributor to export growth during the month

  • Fuel exports jumped 164.5% to $1.8 billion

  • While higher prices were a key driver amid volatility in global energy markets, export volumes also rose sharply for crude oil and fuel

  • Year-to-date, Brazil's trade surplus has widened 34.1% to $71.0 billion

data.title: Week's Best: How to Get In on Anthropic's IPO — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Barron's Advisor Staff

Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic plans to give individual investors a chance to buy shares of the company when it goes public as early as this month. It anticipates allocating a portion of IPO shares to brokerage customers of Charles Schwab, Fidelity, Robinhood Financial (including its TradePMR unit), SoFi, and Morgan Stanley's E*Trade, according to a Nov. 2 regulatory filing. However, a sharp market selloff led by AI stocks this week has some investors questioning if the IPO will take place as planned.

Among other most-read articles:

Charles Schwab to launch more ETFs. Charles Schwab's asset-management unit sees room to further expand its lineup of 34 proprietary exchange-traded funds. Omar Aguilar, head of the company's asset management business, seeks to round out Schwab's ETF lineup with active fixed income and dividend strategies. The expansion plans come as the U.S. ETF industry drew in more than $1.5 trillion in new assets during the first nine months of the year.

Plan for more client spending on health. Advisors know that clients will need to spend a lot on healthcare and medical expenses as they age. Fidelity put the number at $185,500 for retirees today, but that figure doesn't touch the amounts that younger clients will spend throughout adulthood to maintain, monitor, and improve their health, writes Joseph Coughlin, the founder of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's AgeLab. He suggests advisors create three "health portfolios" as part of financial plans to realistically cover a lifetime of health spending.

Market selloff hits financial stocks. Individual investors dumped financial stocks on Thursday, dragging down shares of major brokerage firms and banks such as Robinhood, Webull, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley. Analysts say a broad market selloff would mean less asset growth and could slow the investment banking dealmaking that has boosted bank revenue.

Financial advisor jumps from Merrill to J.P. Morgan. J.P. Morgan Wealth Management has recruited a Los Angeles financial advisor from Merrill Lynch, where she oversaw $940 million in client assets. Tiffany Yu, based in the Century City neighborhood, joined J.P. Morgan on Oct. 30. She is the second high-profile woman J.P. Morgan has recently hired away from Merrill.

Wealth managers weigh in on tokenization. Tokenization of financial assets — where stocks, bonds, funds, and even cash will be recorded as digital tokens on a blockchain, rather than in brokers' ledgers — could mean fast settlement, trading around the clock, fractional ownership, easier access to U.S. markets for overseas investors, and new ways to borrow against holdings. But the hype may be ahead of reality. For this week's Barron's Advisor Big Q, we asked five wealth managers: Is tokenization a big deal for investors? They said yes and explained why.

data.title: Poland aims to cap 2027 natural gas prices for some users funded by windfall levy
data.description:
Poland aims to set a maximum price on natural gas for protected end-users including households in 2027, due to risks related to the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, with compensation to companies financed from a windfall levy on gas importers, the outlines of a draft government bill showed on Friday.

  • The outlines said a significant risk factor is the disruption to the transport of liquefied natural gas through the strait, which has reduced supplies and exerted upward pressure on gas prices in Europe and Asia.

  • According to the proposal, Poland's natural gas supplies were diversified and secure but potential spikes in market prices could negatively impact end-users, such as households, housing cooperatives and associations, and entities that carry out important public utility functions.

  • The draft outlines include a compensation system for gaseous fuel-traders, intended to cover the price difference resulting from the price cap.

  • The compensation would be financed through a windfall levy amounting to 10% of the net revenues of energy companies that hold a licence for the cross-border trading of natural gas and sell high-methane natural gas on the domestic market.
